supersedes.old_reading: large visitor-assemblage contrast with similar self/outcross breeding-system index and negligible autogamy

source_native_facts_requiring_correction.visitor_environment: Guánica has much higher visitation and extreme Apis dominance; Mona has higher visitor richness and a more even assemblage.
source_native_facts_requiring_correction.autogamy: negligible spontaneous self-pollination on both islands; a pollen vector is required
realized_reproductive_performance: On Mona, outcross pollination significantly increased fruit set relative to open pollination (P < 0.001), consistent with pollen limitation under natural conditions.
Multiplicative fitness for open and outcross progenies is lower on Mona than Guánica in the source-native table-level audit.

corrected_observed_pattern: The pollinator assemblage and visitation environment differ strongly. The self/outcross seed-set index is similar between populations and autogamy is negligible, but realized open reproductive performance is not equivalently maintained: Mona shows open-versus-outcross pollen limitation and lower multiplicative fitness. Therefore stability of the breeding-system index must not be relabelled whole-reproduction buffering.
network_context_value: Guaiacum remains highly informative for testing how very different visitor assemblages map into direct effective service, but this mapping explains realized performance rather than a demonstrated buffered reproductive outcome.
boundary: ISI is a selfing/outcrossing seed-set ratio, not total reproductive dependency or realized reproductive performance. Similar ISI across islands cannot support a buffered/resilient classification when open reproductive performance differs.
claim_boundary: This correction does not identify why Mona has lower realized performance and does not infer an Apis causal effect. Direct visitor-specific effectiveness remains missing.
